rls_class.why: Spec 114 §2 is definitional: everything that is not one of the 10 named Class-A tables, not profiles and not Class D is Class B by default, including tables added after that spec was written — which covers contract_descriptors and surface_descriptors. Class B is ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with zero policies, and per Spec 114 §4 / D1 the Next.js admin route connects as the table owner, so it is outside RLS enforcement entirely.
evidence: docs/specs/00-architecture/114_rls_policy_catalog.md §2 — "everything else is Class B by default — including tables added after this spec is written"

checks.why: A row that fails to parse must render as schema_drift; an orphan quietly dropped from the orphan panel is the defect repeating inside its own detector.
Zero orphans is a claim ("I looked and there are none"), and it must be distinguishable from an unseeded registry — the plausible-zero trap the estate has already paid for.
The LIST profile requires an offline state; on a desktop-only admin page there is no cached projection to render, so this is descriptive and no threshold could bound it.
A 500 must not read as "no orphans".
The kind filter is a parameter of a stable key array, not an object literal.
R-13 direction 2: a component file owned by no surface is the UI-side orphan, and it belongs on this page rather than only in the generator's "Unowned components" section.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM contract_descriptors c WHERE c.descriptor->'consumers' IS NULL
invariants.why: A contract whose consumers[] is NULL rather than [] is unmeasured, not orphaned; conflating the two is how a live route gets deleted.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM contract_descriptors c WHERE jsonb_array_length(coalesce(c.descriptor->'consumers','[]'::jsonb)) = 0
plausibility.why: Two independent sweeps disagree on the orphan count today (17 vs the report's admin-side 8 of 29) — ASK-13 — so the count is rendered with its band rather than asserted, and a sudden move to 0 or to 61 means the seed, not the estate, changed.

limitations.what: The LIST required-field profile in Spec 126 §3.1 mandates list.item_archetype, list.pagination and list.recycling, and surface.schema.json has no property for any of them (the top level and every category are additionalProperties:false).
limitations.measured: Every allOf block in scripts/surfaces/_schema/surface.schema.json is `"then": true` — the archetype profiles are declared in prose in Spec 126 §3.1 and enforced by nothing, so these fields cannot be declared here and are not caught missing either.

limitations.what: The orphan count this page renders is contested.
limitations.measured: Spec 126 §2.2.1 P8 records two sweeps disagreeing — 5 of 29 /api/admin/* uncalled by one count, 8 of 29 by the report's, and the census's own 17-contract list adds pipelines/history and pipelines/schedules. Reconciling them is ASK-13 and is explicitly NOT resolved by Spec 126.

notes: Report §1.1 row 19 and §3.2 (verdict BUILD, 'same query, no new dependency'). Reads no DB table — the same descriptor join as admin_contract_fanout, inverted. Measured defects it makes visible: the 17 zero-call-site contracts and 13 no-contract surfaces, with /api/leads/view as row 1 (153L, a live atomic-CTE meter, whitelisted in route-guard.ts:122, 44 test cases across 9 describe blocks, zero production callers, and a consequently unreachable paywall branch at PaywallScreen.tsx:153); plus the admin-side re-measurement of 8 of 29 /api/admin/* route files with no static caller. DESIGNED, NOT MEASURED. UNDECIDED: the orphan COUNT itself is ASK-13 (two sweeps disagree, 5 vs 8 of 29 admin routes, plus a 17-contract census list) and Spec 126 §2.2.1 P8 states outright that "that disagreement is not resolved here" — so the page renders the count with its band rather than asserting one. The `offline` state is declared because the LIST profile requires it, at severity INFO: a desktop admin page has no cached projection, so the honest posture is descriptive, not a threshold.
